sections.title: About the role
paras: Applied Intuition's Digital Proving Grounds (DPGs) give the Department of War a vendor-neutral place to test autonomous systems from many companies together, against a real mission, before they reach the field. A DPG covers the full path from software-in-the-loop (SIL) simulation to hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), live-virtual-constructive (LVC), and live exercises. Teams find integration problems in simulation, where fixes take hours, instead of at a live event, where they take weeks.

DPGs run on Axion, Applied's defense toolchain, with Axion Sim at the core. Applied ran VREX for the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, a DPG that put air, surface, and undersea vehicles from different vendors on one mission. CDAO then selected Applied to build the platform for Autonomy Factory, which brings this approach to programs across the Department of War on autonomy.mil .

The technology works in programs. The next step is a product that program offices, test organizations, and mission engineers choose, adopt, and come back to, without Applied engineers supporting events. As the Product Manager for Digital Proving Grounds, you will own the product strategy, roadmap, and requirements for DPGs and Axion Sim. This is an individual-contributor role. You will work as the product peer to the engineering lead for Axion Sim and drive outcomes through influence across engineering, design, business development, and delivery.

sections.title: At Applied Intuition, you will
bullets: Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for DPGs and Axion Sim. Decide what becomes repeatable product and what stays program-specific work.

Find product-market fit. Run discovery with program offices, test and evaluation organizations, mission engineers, and autonomy vendors. Learn who buys, what they need to prove, and what brings them back for the next event. Work with business development and capture to turn what you learn into offers that win programs.

Define the sim-to-live workflow. Shape how a team goes from a mission and its concept of operations to test scenarios, then to SIL at scale, HIL rig checkout, LVC, and live events, with results that carry across each stage.

Set the simulation roadmap with engineering. Make the calls on fidelity versus speed, sensor and communications modeling, scale to hundreds or thousands of agents, co-simulation with government tools, and a self-serve experience in the cloud and on accredited networks.
Build on shared platform components. Work with other Axion product leads so DPGs use common pieces (simulation, campaigns, metrics, jobs) instead of separate versions.
Write clear requirements and define success metrics. Make the scope trade-offs that keep engineering on the work that matters most for upcoming programs and events.
Shape the experience with design. Partner with design on the tools that test planners, vendors, and government evaluators use every day.

Represent the product. Communicate strategy, status, risk, and trade-offs to Applied leadership and to customers. Present at test events, program reviews, and industry events. Expect to travel about 25% of the time to customer sites, test ranges, and events.

Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it.

Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there.

You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion's AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily.

sections.title: RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES
paras: Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it.

Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not.

The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem.

sections.title: TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS
paras: Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves:
We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires.
bullets: Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior
Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything
Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications

Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation
Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them
Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS

Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone.
Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters

You’ll also work to automate and improve the reactive work that exists today, so that more of your time goes to proactive outreach and campaign development. Velocity is evolving quickly, and you’ll execute plays consistently while giving feedback that helps us improve them as the segment strategy evolves.
If you’re curious, organized, comfortable with high-volume work, and energized by the idea of building scaled programs that make a measurable difference to customers, this role is for you.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Be a value detective: Use data signals (product usage, seat utilization, admin activity, health score, sentiment, support and survey responses) and efficient insight collection to understand each customer’s goals, identify gaps in value, and properly segment the Velocity portfolio.
Execute methodically around signals: Prioritize your day around tasks and plays in ChurnZero that signals trigger, and quickly execute the associated actions based on what the data tells you.
Capture outcomes and sentiment: Validate customer-stated outcomes and keep account data, sentiment, contacts, and risk records accurate so that programs, risk reviews, and teammates can rely on them.
Run programs by segment: Execute plays and campaigns for each customer segment and outcome that drive increasing value from CaptivateIQ over time, with consistent, high-quality follow-through.

Drive adoption along the Golden Path: Guide customers to the features, configurations, and best practices that map to their stated outcome in our Value Framework, partnering closely with our Value Engineer and Education teams.

Scale through multi-channel communication: Create and deploy 1:many programmatic communications – in-app messages, email, Slack, webinars, and cohort-based adoption campaigns – that connect customers to the right resources at the right time.

Connect live where it counts: Host group office hours and run targeted live outreach to customers who need a human conversation, such as new admins, low-adoption accounts, and customers working toward a new outcome.

Manage the inbound queue efficiently: Work customer questions and requests through a queue-based, round-robin model with consistent quality and response times, and flag the patterns that should be automated or self-served back to Product, Education and Support.

sections.title: Product Culture
paras: We are organized into small, durable product teams that develop solutions in specific domains. Our teams are cross-functional — product, design, and engineering work so closely together that we call ourselves DevPro and rarely meet in functional silos. We focus on outcomes over output, which means we engage users early, validate hypotheses through research and prototyping, and iterate rapidly toward high-confidence solutions.

We expect AI tools like Claude Cowork and Claude Code to be central to product managers’’ workflows — as on-demand collaborators that help explore ideas quickly, stress-test assumptions, and move from problem to prototype faster. This is not about replacing PM judgment; it is about using AI to expand what is possible within the constraints of appetite and scope.

sections.title: How We Work — please read this part carefully
paras: This role works differently from most senior product jobs, and the difference is the single biggest predictor of whether someone succeeds here.

Ali, our founder and CEO, sets company priorities. You own the ideas. You will spend part of every day researching competitors, the industry and our users to generate new feature ideas, and you will keep a live Top 3 list of the highest-impact ideas for your area — a new idea only enters by beating one already on it.

You pitch on a single slide with an impact calculation attached. Anything over a week of engineering needs a methodical business case demonstrating ROI. Ali rejects ideas that will not move the number enough to justify the build, and he does so often. The loop is pitch, get rejected, sharpen, re-pitch — continuously, alongside delivery.
